topics.label: Lecture Introduction and Learning Objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the lecturer, the structure of the cancer lecture series, and the core learning outcomes for the session.

topics.label: Conceptual Drivers of Cancer: Intrinsic Mutational Processes and Population Epidemiology
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics establish the foundational concepts of cancer development by exploring the balance between endogenous 'bad luck' mutations, genetic predispositions, and environmental exposures across global populations.

topics.label: Mechanisms of Chemical, Biological, and Physical Carcinogenesis and Tumor Promotion
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine specific carcinogenic agents and the molecular mechanisms by which they induce cancer through direct mutagenesis, xenobiotic metabolic activation, tissue-specific activity, developmental timing, or promotional chronic inflammation.

topics.label: Methodologies for Detecting and Proving Carcinogenicity
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the experimental and observational methodologies used to identify and evaluate carcinogens, ranging from whole-genome mutational signatures and biobanks to animal models and the Ames test.

topics.label: Lecture Conclusion and Everyday Risk-Benefit Decisions
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic delivers concluding lecture remarks reflecting on real-world cancer risk appraisal and practical risk-benefit tradeoffs.
